miniPosts.title: Kleingarten in Berlin: Where the 70,000 Plots Are and How the Wait Really Works
miniPosts.summary: Berlin has 70,390 allotment plots in 1,038 colonies, but Pankow holds over ten thousand and Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg 228. Where the plots actually are, who runs the waiting lists, what the takeover really costs, and the registration move to make this week.

miniPosts.title: Berlin Water Hardness: What Your Postcode Says About the Scale in Your Kettle
miniPosts.summary: Every Berlin postcode runs officially hard water, but a kettle in Wedding and one in Köpenick do not scale at the same speed. The official per-postcode ranges, mapped, with the dishwasher setting, the detergent column and the descaling rhythm that follow.
miniPosts.alt: The two brick towers of the former Prenzlauer Berg waterworks above the trees of the Wasserturm park in autumn

miniPosts.title: Mushroom Picking Around Berlin: Ten Forests on Your Ticket and the Rules Before the Pan
miniPosts.summary: Small amounts for your own pan are legal in both Berlin and Brandenburg forest, porcini and chanterelles carry a personal-use exception, and the free Pilzberatung at the Botanical Garden has checked baskets since 1890. Ten forests from S Rahnsdorf to Chorin, plotted by real travel minutes from Alexanderplatz.

miniPosts.title: Bike Theft in Berlin: Where It Happens, When, and What It Costs
miniPosts.summary: The hour in a Berlin bike theft file is not when the thief turned up, it is when the owner last saw the bike. Read as a parking clock, 31% of losses were locked up between six and ten in the evening, and a third of everything went inside three hours.
miniPosts.alt: Two levels of bicycle racks packed with bikes under the railway structure at Bahnhof Ostkreuz in Berlin

posts.title: Berlin Weekly Markets: Which One Is Open on the Day You Are Free
posts.summary: Berlin does not have one market you can turn up to whenever you like. It has around a hundred of them, each tied to a fixed weekday and a fixed square, and most are folded away by mid-afternoon. Saturday carries nine, Wednesday is the classic morning, Thursday runs latest, Monday has one, and Sunday has none at all. Here is the shape of the market week, and how to pick the one that fits the day you are actually free.
posts.alt: A fruit and vegetable stall under a red and white striped canopy at Winterfeldtplatz market in Berlin

posts.title: Berlin Attraction Tickets: Where to Buy Them and When a Reseller Costs You More
posts.summary: Five of Berlin's most-visited sights have no ticket at all, two of the best are free but only the venue can reserve them, and the paid half of a classic list comes to 93.90 euros. Here is which door each one is sold through, and how to spot the venue's own page before you pay.
